title: 7 Things that a College and Career Ready (CCR) Person Can Do
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. walks through the seven capacities that the Common Core State Standards attribute to a college and career ready person, asking whether the described person would flourish with their gifts in work or college. He translates each into concrete classroom terms: independence with complex texts, building content knowledge, adapting communication to task and audience, comprehending as well as critiquing, valuing evidence, using technology strategically, and understanding other perspectives. Along the way he supplies vivid examples such as the problem of quote bombing and the use of Wikipedia for background rather than proof. The post works as a teacher's translation of a standards page into learning goals for English instruction.
points: Frames the standards through a flourishing question: will the graduate this page describes thrive in work and college?
Turns abstract descriptors into observable behaviors, such as handling an unfamiliar technical text without a teacher holding their hand.
Names quote bombing, dropping in evidence without explaining its use, as a specific failure of valuing evidence.
Insists on pairing comprehension with critique, and treats technology as a tool rather than a shiny object.
Rejects both stereotyping and relativism in the call to understand other cultures.
quotes: CCR people can, without having their hand held by a teacher, comprehend a diverse array of complex texts, and, using these texts, they can make sensible arguments and communicate complicated information (sounds like the reading anchor standards).
Essentially, these people enjoy accumulating knowledge and grappling with it through writing, speaking, blogging, chatting, letter-writing, Skyping, etc.

CCR humans understand that communication must change to meet the situation at hand. If they’re trying to gain the boss’ support for an idea, they will communicate one way, but if they are trying to articulate insights gained from an experiment, they will communicate in another way.
This one is easy to skip over, but think about it: most people are quick to do one or the other of these, but not both.

In other words, they don’t just do what I call “quote bombing” — where you drop in a quote that backs up your argument without any explanation of how it does so — but instead they make clear what a given piece of evidence is being used for.
Short explanation: they use Wikipedia for developing background knowledge, not for proving a point in an argument.
Basically, a CCR person sees technology as a tool, not a shiny object or an omniscient benefactor.
